title: Committed default DJANGO_SECRET_KEY in shipped prod compose
rationale: Root cause is the committed literal default in the compose interpolation `${SO_DJANGO_SECRET_KEY:-<literal>}` at docker-compose-prod-postgres.yml:85, not the Django sink. backend/config/settings/base.py:29 does `SECRET_KEY = env("DJANGO_SECRET_KEY")` with no Python fallback, so whatever compose resolves becomes the live key. If the operator never sets SO_DJANGO_SECRET_KEY, the `:-` fallback supplies the world-readable committed key, which signs sessions and password-reset tokens — an attacker who knows it can forge them. The fix changes `:-` (substitute-if-unset) to `:?message` (Docker Compose error-if-unset-or-empty). This enforces that the operator must provide a per-deployment key; `docker compose up` aborts with the error message instead of silently booting with the known key. No secret value remains in the file. Note: the exposed key in git history still needs rotation operationally — that is out of scope for a code diff.
variants_checked: Same literal `${SO_DJANGO_SECRET_KEY:-NxYPEF5l...}` pattern present in docker-compose-prod-mysql.yml:85 and docker-compose-prod-test.yml:52 (sibling shipped prod compose files — same bug, outside this finding's scoped file f006; should be fixed by the same one-line change there). docker-compose-prod-postgres.yml:86 FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY has the identical committed-literal-default antipattern (encrypts stored fields) and warrants the same `:?` treatment, but it is a distinct secret and outside f006's scope, so I left it untouched and flag it here. charts/secobserve/values.yaml:165 uses `valueFrom: secretKeyRef` — no literal, not vulnerable. dev/unittest/playwright compose files keep literal defaults intentionally and are not prod surfaces.
bypass_considered: Tried: operator exports `SO_DJANGO_SECRET_KEY=` (empty string). With the old `:-` this would still trigger the fallback to the literal; the question is whether my change catches it. The `:?` form (as opposed to `-?`) errors on both unset AND empty, so an empty export also aborts the launch. The remaining residual is an operator who explicitly sets a weak/known value — compose cannot judge key quality, only presence; that is a documentation/entropy concern, not reachable through the interpolation-default path this fix closes.
test_note: No test added. The project's test suite (backend/unittests/) is a Django/Python unittest suite with no harness that parses or validates docker-compose YAML env defaults. A regression test would require introducing a new YAML/grep or shell test category foreign to the repo's conventions, which exceeds the minimal-diff mandate. The change is also self-verifying at runtime: `docker compose -f docker-compose-prod-postgres.yml config` (or `up`) now exits non-zero with the error message when SO_DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is unset, whereas before it silently substituted the committed key.
review_reason: The single hunk at docker-compose-prod-postgres.yml:85 replaces the hardcoded `DJANGO_SECRET_KEY` fallback (`${SO_DJANGO_SECRET_KEY:-NxYP...}`) with the fail-closed `${SO_DJANGO_SECRET_KEY:?...}` form, removing the embedded secret at its root and forcing operators to supply one rather than suppressing the finding. No new parsing, trusted input, or weakened validation is introduced; failing startup when the var is unset is strictly more secure. It matches native Compose `${VAR:?}` style and is minimal; the only nit is that the adjacent `FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY` on line 86 (and the same pattern in prod-mysql.yml:85/prod-test.yml:52) carries the identical issue but is out of scope for this line-scoped finding.
